query: For a high-entropy alloy initially designed as a single-phase solid solution, what testable mechanistic hypothesis explains whether and why it loses toughness or undergoes brittle fracture under mechanical loading in demanding engineering service? Define a controlled comparison that would reveal the governing behavior, predict observations relative to the initial baseline, identify the applicable service and loading boundaries, cite supporting prior evidence, and state a result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Uniaxial tensile loading applied along specific crystallographic directions (<110>, <1-12>, <-111>) at varied temperatures (10 K, 300 K, 600 K) and strain rates (10^8 s^-1, 10^9 s^-1, 10^10 s^-1) via molecular dynamics simulation. applied to AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic HEA in as-cast state (FCC + B2 phases) will act through Enhanced L12 ordering (approaching perfect Ni3Al stoichiometry) in FCC domains coupled with the formation of jagged B2/FCC phase boundaries and Elevated APBE and elastic modulus in ordered domains restrict cross-slip and promote planar slip; combined with stress concentration at jagged PB tips, this triggers plastic instability. At higher temperatures, reduced ordering and formation of ductile transition zones along PBs restore ductility., giving A non-monotonic ductile-brittle-ductile transition where ductility is minimized at the aging temperature that maximizes L12 ordering and jagged PB density (600°C) and recovers at higher temperatures (750°C) where ordering is suppressed. relative to Conventional alloys exhibiting classical grain-boundary mediated thermal embrittlement (e.g., temper embrittlement via impurity segregation).
generation.material_initial_state: AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic HEA in as-cast state (FCC + B2 phases)
generation.intervention: Uniaxial tensile loading applied along specific crystallographic directions (<110>, <1-12>, <-111>) at varied temperatures (10 K, 300 K, 600 K) and strain rates (10^8 s^-1, 10^9 s^-1, 10^10 s^-1) via molecular dynamics simulation.
generation.conditions: Aging regime defined by a specific temperature window (approx. 550-750°C) where chemical ordering kinetics and phase boundary evolution are maximized
generation.structural_mediator: Enhanced L12 ordering (approaching perfect Ni3Al stoichiometry) in FCC domains coupled with the formation of jagged B2/FCC phase boundaries
generation.mechanism: Elevated APBE and elastic modulus in ordered domains restrict cross-slip and promote planar slip; combined with stress concentration at jagged PB tips, this triggers plastic instability. At higher temperatures, reduced ordering and formation of ductile transition zones along PBs restore ductility.
generation.predicted_outcome: A non-monotonic ductile-brittle-ductile transition where ductility is minimized at the aging temperature that maximizes L12 ordering and jagged PB density (600°C) and recovers at higher temperatures (750°C) where ordering is suppressed.
generation.baseline: Conventional alloys exhibiting classical grain-boundary mediated thermal embrittlement (e.g., temper embrittlement via impurity segregation)

falsification_experiment.design: Transmission Kikuchi Diffraction (TKD) or TEM observation of dislocation pile-ups and crack initiation specifically at the tips of jagged phase boundaries, with no evidence of intergranular impurity segregation.
measurements: Transmission Kikuchi Diffraction (TKD) or TEM observation of dislocation pile-ups and crack initiation specifically at the tips of jagged phase boundaries, with no evidence of intergranular impurity segregation.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the predicted outcome is not observed relative to the baseline, the hypothesis is rejected.
